findings.summary: CMake install() directives for headers, shared library, static library, pkg-config file, man pages, and cmake config files are not captured as rules_pkg install_files/install_mapped targets in any Bazel BUILD file.
findings.evidence: CMake: CMakeLists.txt exposes SDL_INSTALL, SDL_INSTALL_TESTS, SDL_INSTALL_DOCS, SDL_INSTALL_CPACK options and issues install(TARGETS SDL3-shared SDL3-static ...), install(DIRECTORY include/SDL3 DESTINATION include), install(FILES ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/sdl3.pc DESTINATION lib/pkgconfig), and installs cmake config files to lib/cmake/SDL3. Bazel: MODULE.bazel references rules_pkg but no BUILD.bazel contains pkg_install, install_files, or install_mapped rules; the entire install layout is silently absent.

findings.summary: All ~50 test executables defined in test/CMakeLists.txt are completely absent from the Bazel output. No cc_binary or sh_test targets exist for testautomation, testfile, testgeometry, testgl, testvulkan, or any other SDL test program.
findings.evidence: CMake: test/CMakeLists.txt defines add_sdl_test_executable() for ~50 executables (testautomation, testfile, testgeometry, testgl, testgles2, testvulkan, testaudio, testmouse, testrelative, etc.) with resource file dependencies and install rules. Bazel: elements/sdl/BUILD.bazel, elements/sdl/src/BUILD.bazel, and all other BUILD files contain zero test target definitions — the entire test suite is silently dropped.

findings.summary: CMake conditionally applies a linker version script (SDL3.sym.in via --version-script=) to control symbol visibility on ELF platforms. This check-and-apply step is absent from the Bazel link options, leaving all symbols exported on Linux.
findings.evidence: CMake: CMakeLists.txt ~line 471 calls check_linker_supports_version_file() then appends -Wl,--version-script=${SDL3_SOURCE_DIR}/src/SDL3.sym to the shared library link flags only if the linker supports it. Bazel: elements/sdl/BUILD.bazel linkopts list contains no --version-script entry; SDL3.sym.in is not referenced anywhere in the Bazel workspace.

findings.summary: CMake sets target_compile_features(SDL3-shared PRIVATE c_std_99) and target_compile_features(SDL3-static PRIVATE c_std_99), enforcing C99. The Bazel cc_library has no equivalent conlyopts or copts entry enforcing -std=c99; consuming targets inherit the toolchain default.
findings.evidence: CMake: CMakeLists.txt line ~429 calls target_compile_features(SDL3-shared PRIVATE c_std_99) and similarly for SDL3-static, ensuring the library always compiles as C99 regardless of toolchain default. Bazel: elements/sdl/src/BUILD.bazel copts list does not include -std=c99 or equivalent; cc_library has no c_options attribute set.

findings.summary: CMake exposes an SDL_ASSERTIONS option with five levels (auto/disabled/release/enabled/paranoid) that sets SDL_DEFAULT_ASSERT_LEVEL. The Bazel build config header hardcodes the undef state with no way to select a different assertion level without re-conversion.
findings.evidence: CMake: CMakeLists.txt line 307 defines option(SDL_ASSERTIONS 'Enable internal sanity checks (auto/disabled/release/enabled/paranoid)' 'auto') and lines ~540-556 map each value to a numeric SDL_DEFAULT_ASSERT_LEVEL written into SDL_build_config.h. Bazel: elements/sdl/include-config-relwithdebinfo/build_config/BUILD.bazel write_file() hardcodes '#undef SDL_DEFAULT_ASSERT_LEVEL_CONFIGURED' with no Bazel flag or select() to choose a different level.

findings.summary: CMake sets VERSION and SOVERSION properties on the SDL3-shared target (e.g. VERSION 3.x.y SOVERSION 0), controlling the shared library's soname and compatibility version. The Bazel cc_library has no mechanism to express this, so the built .so has no soname.
findings.evidence: CMake: CMakeLists.txt ~line 447 calls set_target_properties(SDL3-shared PROPERTIES VERSION ${SDL_VERSION} SOVERSION ${SDL_SOVERSION}) producing libSDL3.so.0.y.z with libSDL3.so.0 soname symlink. Bazel: elements/sdl/BUILD.bazel cc_library for the shared variant has no soname attribute; resulting .so will have no soname, breaking ldconfig-based consumers.

findings.summary: All ~13 example executables (renderer-clear, renderer-geometry, audio-simple-playback, demo-snake, etc.) defined in examples/CMakeLists.txt are absent from the Bazel output.
findings.evidence: CMake: examples/CMakeLists.txt defines sdl_add_example_executable() for renderer-clear, renderer-geometry, renderer-primitives, renderer-texture, renderer-present-vsync, audio-simple-playback, audio-simple-capture, demo-snake, demo-woodeneye-008, and others, plus DATAFILES install for sample.bmp, sample.wav. Bazel: no BUILD.bazel file exists under elements/sdl for examples; no cc_binary or data filegroup targets.

findings.summary: CMake generates and installs man pages for every public SDL3 API function via sdlmanpages.cmake. There is no equivalent genrule or build target in the Bazel workspace.
findings.evidence: CMake: cmake/sdlmanpages.cmake is included from CMakeLists.txt and generates man3 pages for SDL functions, controlled by SDL_INSTALL_DOCS and SDL_INSTALL_MAN options; install(FILES ... DESTINATION share/man/man3). Bazel: cmake/sdlmanpages.cmake is not referenced in any BUILD.bazel file; no genrule, expand_template, or write_file target exists for man page generation or install.

findings.summary: CMake uses PRIVATE compile definitions and PRIVATE include directories on SDL3-shared/SDL3-static to prevent them leaking to consumers. The Bazel cc_library places all defines and include paths in defines/includes rather than local_defines/private includes, potentially leaking internal build-time macros to dependent targets.
findings.evidence: CMake: cmake/sdltargets.cmake ~line 105-165 uses target_compile_definitions(SDL3-shared PRIVATE SDL_BUILD_DLL) and target_include_directories(SDL3-shared PRIVATE src/) so internal paths are not propagated. Bazel: elements/sdl/src/BUILD.bazel and elements/sdl/BUILD.bazel use defines = [...] (public) and includes = [...] (exported), so SDL_BUILD_DLL and internal src include paths are exported to all consumers of the cc_library.
